narrative:
The model estimates a 75% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your profile that historically align with employees who eventually depart.

The three factors that most shaped this outlook were, in order: having received other job offers while at the company, your overall career experience, and the length of time you have spent in your present role. 

Having other job opportunities was the strongest influence and pushed the prediction strongly toward leaving. While only 23% of employees predicted to stay had received such offers, you have, which the model sees as a clear signal that you have external options and may be considering them.

Your total years of experience came next and also increased the likelihood of departure. With 6–10 years overall, you sit in a mid-career band where 35% of stayers fall, yet the model interprets this stage as one where people often begin exploring new paths.

Time in your current organization worked in the opposite direction. Spending 6–10 years in the same place (again, 35% of stayers are in this range) slightly pulled the prediction back toward staying, suggesting some loyalty or familiarity.

Taken together, the external opportunities and your career stage outweighed the stabilizing effect of tenure. The organization should discuss retention measures with you, while you may wish to reflect on whether your current path still meets your long-term goals. (248 words)
